processing: Ripe pu-erh from the Menghai Tea Factory: wet-piled Yunnan tea blended to a numbered recipe and pressed into cakes.
harvest_season: Not tied to one picking: factory recipes blend stored material.
appearance_dry: A brown cake of ripe leaf, as usual for Menghai factory cakes.
appearance_liquor: Dark red-brown, as usual for Menghai ripe pu-erh.
appearance_wet: Soft dark brown leaf, as usual for ripe pu-erh.
taste_profile: Little tasting detail is on record; expect the typical Menghai ripe profile of earth, wood and dark sweetness.

brewing.notes: Standard ripe handling: rinse once and use near-boiling water.

vintage_note: Sold as a dated factory cake, with a 2017 pressing among those on the market. As with other Dayi ripe teas, expect a batch code on the wrapper giving the year and run; it can be drunk young and usually softens with a few years of storage.
description:
8562 is a Menghai Tea Factory ripe cake, part of the same numbered family as 7562 and 0562, and far less discussed than either.

Informal explanations read the number as year, main leaf grade and factory. That would make it a 1985 recipe built around grade 6, from Menghai. It is a plausible reading and nothing firmer, since no official explanation of this number is available.

Detailed notes are rare, so assume the typical Menghai ripe style until you have tried it: earth, wood and a dark sweetness, best with very hot water and a quick rinse.

Buy it by pressing year and batch, and try a sample first because so little is written about it.
history: Little is documented about this recipe. The Menghai Tea Factory, which became fully private in 1996 and adopted the Dayi mark, has sold cakes under the number, including a 2017 pressing, but when and why 8562 was created is not established.
